item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 292305
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM EDT Tue Sep 29 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Hanna, located well to the east of Bermuda, and has issued the
final advisory on Post-Tropical Cyclone Fay, located over the
central subtropical Atlantic.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...23.7N 48.2W
ABOUT 1590 MI...2560 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...30 MPH...45 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WSW OR 240 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1011 MB...29.86 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM AST (2100 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone Fay 
was located near latitude 23.7 North, longitude 48.2 West. The 
post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the west-southwest near 12 
mph (19 km/h), and this motion is expected to continue for the next 
couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 30 mph (45 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Little change in strength is forecast, and Fay is forecast to 
dissipate in a day or so.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1011 mb (29.86 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. Additional information on this system can be 
found in High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, 
under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and online at 
ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Fay Forecast Discussion Number 39
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM AST Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 292034
TCDAT1
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Fay Discussion Number  39
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
500 PM AST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
Fay's time as a tropical cyclone has faded away. An earlier 
scatterometer pass showed that the system had weakened with maximum 
winds around 25 kt, and that the low-level center was becoming less 
defined. While occasional bursts of convection may continue, the 
convection has not been organized in several hours. Thus, the system 
is being designated as a post-tropical cyclone with an initial 
intensity of 25 kt.
 
The post-tropical cyclone will continue to move generally 
west-southwestward at around 10 kt, steered along the southern 
periphery of the mid-level ridge located over the central Atlantic. 
The system should continue to gradually weaken and is expected to 
dissipate into an open trough in about a day or so. The latest NHC 
track and intensity forecast is similar to the previous advisory and 
lies near the latest consensus aids.
 
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. Additional information on this system can be 
found in High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, 
under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and online at 
ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php

...HANNA HOLDING STEADY WHILE MAINTAINING A SOUTHEASTWARD TRACK...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM GMT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...33.7N 43.6W
ABOUT 1230 MI...1980 KM E OF BERMUDA
ABOUT 975 MI...1565 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SE OR 130 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM GMT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Hanna was 
located near latitude 33.7 North, longitude 43.6 West. Hanna is 
moving toward the southeast near 12 mph (19 km/h). This 
motion is forecast to continue with a decrease in forward speed 
through morning, followed by a turn to the east-northeast.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual weakening is expected during the next couple of days, 
and Hanna is likely to become a post-tropical cyclone tonight or 
Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Hanna Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM GMT Wed Sep 30 2026 
000
WTNT43 KNHC 300235
TCDAT3
 
Tropical Storm Hanna Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL082026
300 AM GMT Wed Sep 30 2026

Visible and infrared satellite imagery shows that the low-level 
center remains exposed to the west of the main convection area. 
The convective pattern has become even more elongated west-east, 
likely influenced by the nearby frontal boundary. A 0032 UTC 
METOP-C scatterometer pass shows peak winds of 33 kt in the 
northeast quadrant. The latest TAFB Dvorak fix was T2.5/35 kt, 
aligning well with the mostly unchanged UW-CIMSS objective 
estimates. Based on all of these data, the initial intensity remains 
35 kt.
 
The initial motion remains southeastward, now 130/10 kt, as Hanna is 
moving along the southern edge of the mid-latitude westerlies to the 
southwest of a large trough over the northeastern Atlantic. During 
the next 12–24 h, the flow near the cyclone will become more 
west-to-east, and as Hanna weakens vertically a low-level ridge 
centered south of the Azores will become the main steering 
influence. This should result in the cyclone, or its remnants, 
turning east-northeastward. The updated NHC forecast track was 
largely unchanged from the previous advisory and remains close to 
the corrected multi-model consensus (HCCA).

Hanna is forecast to gradually weaken as it persists in a 
moisture-starved environment, with moderate to strong vertical wind 
shear prevailing over the next 48 to 72 h. The latest GFS/ECMWF 
simulated satellite imagery now forecasts the system to stop 
producing convection in 24-36 h, at which time it would degenerate 
into a remnant low. After that, the remnant low is expected to open 
into a trough by 96 h.  However, it is possible that the system 
becomes a post-tropical system sooner if it merges with the nearby 
front.
